blocks.text: Wrapper Methods introduced the genuine general idea, training real models to directly measure feature subset performance, while flagging that trying every possible subset exhaustively is genuinely impractical. Forward selection is the genuine first, most intuitive answer to that problem, building a feature subset up gradually, one feature at a time, always choosing whichever addition helps the most at each individual step.

This topic covers exactly how forward selection starts from an empty feature set, how it evaluates every remaining candidate feature at each round using cross validation, how it decides when to stop adding features, the real, genuine limitation this greedy, step by step approach carries, and how it compares in computational cost to the exhaustive search wrapper methods explicitly avoid.
1. Starting From Nothing
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421231-880548689.png

Forward selection genuinely begins with an empty feature set, zero features selected at all. This is genuinely the defining starting point that gives this strategy its name, building up from nothing, in direct contrast to the next topic, backward elimination, which genuinely starts from the complete opposite direction.
Beginning empty means the very first round genuinely has to identify which single feature, on its own, contributes the most to real model performance, exactly the first concrete step covered next.
2. Trying Every Remaining Candidate
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421231-840243166.png

At every round, forward selection genuinely takes every feature not yet selected, and tries adding each one, individually, to the current feature set, training an actual model and evaluating its genuine real performance using cross validation for every single candidate addition. If 10 features remain, that genuinely means 10 separate models get trained and evaluated in that one round alone.

This exhaustive testing within each individual round is genuinely what makes forward selection a real wrapper method, exactly as covered in the previous topic, every candidate addition genuinely gets judged by real, actual model performance, not a generic statistical score.
3. Picking the Best Addition Each Round

blocks.alt: Picking the Best Addition Each Round
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421232-440157327.png

Once every genuine candidate addition has been tried for that round, whichever one produced the genuinely best real performance gets added permanently to the selected feature set. That feature now genuinely stays in the set for every remaining round, the process moves forward to the next round with one fewer remaining candidate to consider.

This genuine, permanent commitment at each step is exactly what makes this strategy greedy, once a feature is added, it is never reconsidered or removed later, a real, important limitation covered directly further in this topic.
4. A Worked Example
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421232-471805915.png
Using scikit-learn SequentialFeatureSelector with the forward direction shows this entire process applied directly, letting the library handle the round by round evaluation automatically.

code.content:
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import SequentialFeatureSelector
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({
    "square_feet": [900, 1200, 1500, 1800, 2100, 2400],
    "bedrooms": [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5],
    "shoe_size_unrelated": [8, 9, 7, 10, 8, 9],
})
y = pd.Series([0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1])

selector = SequentialFeatureSelector(
    LogisticRegression(), n_features_to_select=2, direction="forward", cv=3
)
selector.fit(X, y)

print("Selected features:", X.columns[selector.get_support()].tolist())

blocks.text: scikit-learn genuinely handles the entire round by round process internally here, trying each candidate addition, evaluating it with cross validation, and committing to the genuinely best one each round, exactly as described above, correctly landing on square_feet and bedrooms while leaving the deliberately irrelevant shoe size column out.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Set cv to a genuinely reasonable number of folds, 3 to 5 for most datasets, when running SequentialFeatureSelector. Too few folds risks an unreliable performance estimate at every single round of this search.

blocks.text: 5. When to Stop Adding Features
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421232-408306525.png

Forward selection genuinely needs a stopping rule, otherwise it would simply keep adding every remaining feature until none are left. The genuine, most common approach sets a fixed target feature count in advance, exactly n_features_to_select in the worked example above, stopping once that count is reached regardless of whether further additions might still help slightly.

An alternative, genuinely more adaptive approach stops as soon as adding another feature no longer improves real performance by a meaningful amount, letting the data itself determine the final feature count rather than fixing it in advance.

blocks.text: 6. A Real, Genuine Limitation: Greedy, Not Global

blocks.alt: A Real, Genuine Limitation: Greedy, Not Global
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421232-534656476.png

Because forward selection genuinely commits permanently to each feature the moment it is added, it can genuinely miss the actual best overall combination, a feature that looked only mildly useful early on, and was therefore never selected, might have combined powerfully with a feature added several rounds later, a combination this greedy process genuinely never gets the chance to discover, since it cannot backtrack and reconsider earlier decisions.

This is a genuinely real, honest limitation shared by greedy algorithms generally, forward selection finds a genuinely good, locally sensible feature set efficiently, but offers no genuine guarantee that it finds the actual best possible one across every conceivable combination.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Forward selection genuinely trades a guarantee of finding the best possible feature subset for real, practical efficiency. It finds a genuinely good subset quickly, not necessarily the single best one that exists.

blocks.text: 7. Computational Cost Compared to Exhaustive Search

With n total features, the first round genuinely tries n candidates, the second round genuinely tries n minus 1 remaining candidates, and so on, a genuinely far smaller number of total models trained than the combinatorial explosion of trying every possible subset, exactly the real cost problem flagged back in Wrapper Methods.

This is genuinely why forward selection, and the other search strategies covered in this module, exist at all, they trade the guaranteed global optimum of exhaustive search for a real, practical, genuinely tractable amount of computation.

blocks.text: 8. Forward Selection Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: Forward Selection Versus What Comes Next
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421233-969185125.png

Forward selection genuinely builds a feature set up from nothing, one addition at a time. The next topic takes the genuine, complete opposite approach, starting from every feature available and removing them one at a time instead, offering a genuinely different perspective on the same underlying search problem.

Backward Elimination, covered next, starts from the full feature set and genuinely removes the least useful feature at each round, a mirror image strategy worth understanding directly alongside this one.

items: Forward selection genuinely starts from an empty feature set and builds it up one feature at a time.
At each round, every remaining candidate feature is genuinely tried and evaluated with cross validation.
The genuinely best performing addition each round gets added permanently to the selected set.
Stopping happens at a genuine fixed target count, or adaptively once no further real improvement occurs.
This greedy approach genuinely cannot backtrack, and is not guaranteed to find the actual best overall subset.
The next topic, Backward Elimination, covers the genuine mirror image strategy, starting full and removing features instead.
